- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.16 or 79.68), then corrects with a lagged downward bias.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion toward recent lower levels.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth; fails to capture volatility or sudden reversals in the true outcome.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent high prices (e.g., >80).
- When true outcome shows a sharp upward move (e.g., 81+), model lags and underestimates the peak.
- Forecasts often ignore the influence of recent low prices (e.g., 75–76) and overreact to recent highs.
